title: Install standup scrapbook — Sept 2026
body:
Weekly install scrapbook (freeform notes + decisions)

Context: rolling field installs for three customers this sprint (Nimbus, Halcyon Health, and Kestrel Financial). Mix of VPC and on-prem rack installs. This doc collects standup bullets, quick triage traces, and concrete next steps — intended for the install squad + solutions-engineering to sync asynchronously.

HIGHLIGHTS
- Nimbus (VPC): core control-plane up in eu-west-1; inference nodes passing smoke tests at 90% capacity. Observed intermittent 502s from gateway -> router during high batch loads.
- Halcyon (on-prem): on-site installation completed; persistent L1 TLS handshake failures between customer load balancer and our ingress. Root cause appears to be MTU mismatch + packet fragmentation at L2.
- Kestrel (hybrid): initial KV cache replication succeeded, but the quantized model binary failed checksum after the first warmup sequence — likely s3 multipart ordering vs local fs write concurrency.

RECENT STANDUP BULLETS (raw)
- Priya: Nimbus 502s spike when seq_len > 1024 with batching=auto; disabling continuous batching for affected routes stabilizes. Temporary patch rolled to canary.
- Lian: Halcyon NICs set to jumbo frames; customer infra team reverted to default 1500 on our ask — still failing. Captured tcpdump and forwarded to networking for deep-dive.
- Ethan: Kestrel artifact rewrite: adding per-chunk verify + retry to uploader. Re-run tomorrow.
- Sofia: CS flagged that Halcyon has security review deadline next Fri; need concrete mitigation and risk statement.
- Marcus: updated install checklist with new certificate rotation step and clarified expected cipher suites for HAProxy -> router.

BLOCKERS & TRIAGE NOTES
- Intermittent gateway 502s (Nimbus):
  * Symptom: spike in 502s correlated with request bursts for long-sequence generation.
  * Hypothesis: batching optimization + kernel selection path causes transient memory pressure and connection drop.
  * Evidence: kube OOMKills x0, but router process logs show rapid accept->close cycles. Heap/stack traces attached in JIRA-PDEP-1183.
  * Workaround: force-route affected endpoints to non-batched instance pool; disable kernel fusion optimization for route.
  * Next: instrument per-request KV cache pressure metrics; assign to Lian for metric + dashboard (due 2026-09-14).

- TLS handshake failures (Halcyon):
  * Symptom: client handshake timeout; alerts show packets with DF bit set then ICMP fragmentation-needed replies.
  * Hypothesis: MTU mismatch somewhere in middlebox chain + offload interactions on Broadcom NICs.
  * Actions taken: captured full tcpdump (segmented) and provided PCAP to customer network team. Confirmed packet sizes ~1600 bytes being sent.
  * Temporary: force app to set MSS clamp on egress; request customer to add path MTU discovery exemptions.
  * Escalation path: if customer cannot approve changes, open support ticket with switch vendor and move install window.

- Model binary checksum flake (Kestrel):
  * Symptom: artifact checksum mismatch reported by verifier during warm-up on second run.
  * Root cause (likely): concurrent multipart uploads occasionally reorder completion markers; downloader wrote file before finalization signal.
  * Fix: add strong rename/atomic commit step in artifact downloader + retry-on-verify. Patch in PR 421. Deploy to canary.

DECISIONS MADE
- Rollback plan for Nimbus: keep canary with disabled batching for 24h. If error rate <1% and latency SLO met, stage gradual re-enable with throttled batch sizes.
- Halcyon: do not change customer's LB config without signed approval. Proceed with app-level MSS clamp as short-term mitigation and provide security risk statement to CS.
- Kestrel: require checksum verification at unpack time in all install pipelines going forward. Add test case in release gating.

ACTION ITEMS (owner | item | due)
- Lian Chen | Add KV cache pressure and request size histogram to install dashboard; create alert for >75% cache occupancy | 2026-09-14
- Ethan Morales | Merge artifact atomic-commit change and run full onprem install simulation in CI | 2026-09-13
- Sofia Alvarez | Draft security risk statement + mitigation summary for Halcyon and route to customer success for signoff | 2026-09-12
- Marcus Ito | Update on-prem install checklist to include NIC offload verification, MSS clamp note, and capture steps for tcpdump | 2026-09-11
- Priya Kapoor | Schedule vendor-escalation call if Halcyon cannot test path MTU changes by 2026-09-15 | 2026-09-13

NOTES TO SELF / WORKING THOUGHTS
- Evaluate whether disabling kernel fusion is always safe for seq_len > 1024; might hide perf regressions. Add unit test that simulates request distribution.
- Consider adding a preflight MTU check in the install-runbook that sends oversize UDP/ICMP probes to detect fragmentation early. This would have caught Halcyon earlier. Low-effort, high-impact.
- Revisit artifact push ordering: maybe use S3 object tagging + finalize marker to avoid reliance on eventual consistency in our downloader logic.

COMMUNICATIONS LOG / CUSTOMER NOTES
- Halcyon (2026-09-09): on-site engineer reported: "we see the TLS errors only when multiple concurrent warmups run; single-run warm-up is fine." Escalated to network team.
- Nimbus (2026-09-10): slack thread #nimbus-install — customer accepted temporary throughput reduction for stability testing window.
- Kestrel (2026-09-08): posted PR 421 link and asked for manual verification after patch.

FOLLOW-UPS FOR NEXT STANDUP
- Confirm Nimbus canary health after 24h. (Priya)
- Halcyon MTU mitigation acceptance or vendor escalation decision. (Sofia + Marcus)
- Kestrel artifact verification pass in CI + sign-off. (Ethan)

ATTACHMENTS / ARTIFACTS (links)
- tcpdump-halcyon-0909.pcap (uploaded to shared drive, see linked_artifacts)
- JIRA-PDEP-1183 (502 spikes investigation)
